flashcards.q: Name the four distinct SageMaker inference products and their core cost/latency profile.
flashcards.a: Real-Time Endpoints: always-on, sub-second, billed per instance-hour regardless of load. Serverless Inference: scale-to-zero, 1-5s cold start, billed per invocation. Async Inference: queued, up to 1GB payload/1hr processing, scales to zero. Batch Transform: offline job, no live endpoint, billed per instance-hour for job duration.

flashcards.q: What is JumpStart, and why isn't it a fifth SageMaker inference product?
flashcards.a: JumpStart is a model zoo/deployment accelerator that pre-packages open models for one-click or one-API deployment onto one of the four actual inference products (Real-Time, Serverless, Async, or Batch Transform) — it's not a distinct serving mode itself.

flashcards.q: Contrast the cost-model shape of Bedrock on-demand versus self-hosted vLLM.
flashcards.a: Bedrock on-demand is linear in actual token usage (pay per token processed). Self-hosting is a step function in provisioned capacity (pay per instance-hour regardless of utilization) — at low/spiky usage Bedrock wins, at high steady utilization self-hosting's effective per-token cost drops below Bedrock's.

Standard: baseline pricing/performance. Priority: premium over Standard for preferential queue treatment, up to ~25% better output-tokens-per-second latency. Flex: discounted vs Standard, for workloads tolerant of being queued behind Standard-tier traffic during high load (batch-like, non-urgent multi-step work).

flashcards.q: What is Bedrock Provisioned Throughput, and where do you find its pricing?
flashcards.a: Reserved dedicated capacity (in 'model units') for a 1- or 6-month commitment, guaranteeing throughput independent of the shared on-demand pool. AWS generally does not publish per-model-unit rates on the standard pricing page; enterprise customers are directed to their account team for a quote.

flashcards.q: What's the directionally-estimated crossover point where self-hosting starts beating Bedrock on cost, and what caveat must accompany it?
flashcards.a: Roughly 10,000-20,000 requests/day or a few thousand dollars/month in API spend, per industry estimates — but this is heavily workload-dependent (token length, latency SLA, traffic steadiness) and should never be quoted as a precise universal number.

flashcards.q: What does the 'fully-loaded' cost of self-hosting include beyond the raw EC2 bill?
flashcards.a: Engineer-hours for capacity planning and on-call, ongoing vLLM/CUDA/driver upgrade maintenance, building autoscaling that reacts as fast as a hosted provider's shared fleet, and the opportunity cost of the team's attention.

flashcards.q: How do Bedrock and SageMaker compare to self-hosting on data residency?
flashcards.a: Bedrock and SageMaker are broadly similar: both AWS-operated within the customer's account/region boundary, with AWS's stated policy of not training on customer data or moving it out of region. Self-hosting is stricter — the literal serving process runs on infrastructure the org directly controls, which some regulated environments require as a hard line.

flashcards.q: Compare lock-in across Bedrock, SageMaker, and self-hosted.
flashcards.a: Bedrock: high — prompts/evals/fine-tuning built against AWS's specific model catalog and API. SageMaker: medium — AWS-infrastructure-specific, but the model artifact/container itself is portable. Self-hosted: low technical lock-in (same container runs anywhere), though the organizational investment in your own ops tooling is real.

flashcards.q: What happens if traffic exceeds your Bedrock on-demand quota during a spike?
flashcards.a: Requests are throttled (fail closed) rather than autoscaled, since quota increases require a support-ticket request subject to AWS capacity and are not instant — proactively request quota increases before a known traffic event.

flashcards.q: A SageMaker Real-Time Endpoint has low, intermittent traffic and a high bill. What's the fix?
flashcards.a: Real-Time Endpoints bill per instance-hour regardless of utilization — switch to Serverless Inference (scale-to-zero, pay per invocation) for intermittent/unpredictable traffic, or Async Inference if payloads/processing time don't fit a synchronous model.

flashcards.q: When is SageMaker the right middle-ground choice over both Bedrock and plain self-hosted EC2/EKS?
flashcards.a: When you need full control over the model artifact/container (custom or fine-tuned open-weight model) but don't want to own infrastructure orchestration (provisioning, health checks, autoscaling wiring) yourself — SageMaker gives you AWS-managed infra around a model you fully control.
